newsitem.title: UK: Britain plans glittering royal golden wedding.
newsitem.headline: Britain plans glittering royal golden wedding.

text.p: Britain's Queen Elizabeth and the Duke of Edinburgh will attend a thanksgiving service at London's Westminster Abbey in November to mark their golden wedding anniversary, Buckingham Palace announced on Wednesday.
The service on November 20 in the church where they were married is part of a glittering series of events to mark the royal couple's 50 years together.
It will be preceded on November 19 by a lunch given by the Lord Mayor of London and followed by a lunch hosted by the government of Prime Minister Tony Blair at the nearby Banqueting Hall.
On July 5, the queen will attend the Royal Pageant of the Horse at Windsor, a festival bringing together hundreds of horses in one of the biggest events of its kind in Britain.

On July 15, the queen and the Duke of Edinburgh will give a garden party at Buckingham Palace for 4,000 couples who were also married in 1947. Each of the couples were winners in a ballot entered by more than 40,000.

And on November 14, the queen will give a "thank you' reception for 1,500 people closely involved in restoring Windsor Castle after it was badly damaged by fire in 1992, the year she described as her "annus horribilis".
Since then the marriage of her eldest son Charles to Princess Diana has ended and his brother Andrew's marriage to the Duchess of York has also finished in divorce.
